editorial.html:
Harborlight Literacy Project · FY2027 budget request

Staff estimate a sixth site would cut Harborlight’s waitlist in half

Staff want the board to approve a $1,610,000 FY2027 budget that opens a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. The board votes on October 21.

287
Adults still waiting for a spot at the end of FY2026

The request

The budget adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year and cut the waitlist in half.

Demand keeps growing

Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in FY2026, up from 936 the year before. Even so, 287 adults were still on the waitlist at year end, most at Eastgate and Riverside. The average wait was nine weeks.

Results for learners

Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in Harborlight’s history. 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 hours and stayed 14 months on average.

Budget and reserves

FY2026 operating expenses were $1,420,000, with 81 percent going to programs. Foundation grants brought in $640,000, individual donors $388,000 and the city contract $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237. Reserves cover 3.2 months, below the board’s 4-month goal.
